From: David Boucher, Superintendent
Wastewater Department
Re: Vogelsang Sludge Transfer Pump Purchase
E. Motion: To approve the purchase of three (3) Vogelsang brand sludge transfer pumps from
Wescor Associates, Inc, of Wrentham, MA, in an amount not to exceed $60,180. Funding
will be through: Department: 169 Wastewater; Fund: Wastewater; Account
Classification: WERF.
Attachments: Vendor Quote
Discussion: The Wastewater Facility uses four Vogelsang sludge transfer pumps to transfer sludge
from the sludge holding tanks to the dewatering presses on the upper floor in the
building. These pumps require routine maintenance and replacement of wear items
regularly. At a certain point, the pumps get worn beyond repair and require replacement
in order to pump at their needed capacity. Three pumps can be used at any given time,
with the fourth serving as redundancy. As such, three (3) new Vogelsang pumps should
be ordered and replaced. This equipment is inventoried and budgeted thru the Wastewater
Equipment Replacement Fund (WERF) list, and would replace WERF Asset ID SPFP-1,
SPFP-2, and SPFP-3.
Wescor Associates, Inc, is the local representative of Vogelsang and this is an in-kind
replacement, making this a sole source purchase. We are requesting the purchase be made
from Wescor Associates, Inc for a total cost of $60,180.

To: Board of Public Works Meeting Date: June 26, 2025
From: David Boucher, Superintendent
Wastewater Department
Re: SCADA System Upgrade
B. Motion: To approve the SCADA System Upgrade purchase and installation with Electrical
Installations, LLC, in an amount not to exceed $271,985. Funding will be through:
Department: 169 Wastewater; Fund: Bond; Activity: SCADA upgrades.
Attachments: Vendor pricing agreement
Discussion: The Wastewater Treatment Facility has extensive equipment throughout the Facility and
pump stations that are controlled through our SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data
Acquisition) system. These controls allow for real time data collection, monitoring, and
control. The system is programmed to automatically regulate pumps and chemical
dosing, as well as other needs. It helps the Facility work efficiently, with better control,
optimizing energy use, manual labor, and ensuring consistent permit compliance.
The SCADA system is computer and software based, requiring it to be updated
constantly. We are currently looking at a full system upgrade, including the appropriate
hardware, as well as security upgrades. This work is in conjunction with the City’s IT
department, where appropriate.
Currently the wastewater facility uses Electrical Installations, LLC for all of our SCADA
needs. They have the most up to date program and have performed all integrations for the
current and past projects, dating back the last seven years. They are familiar with the
system and can provide the work needed in the most efficient manner. We are
recommending them for this work.

Please see attached communications from Michael Rush, Superintendent Fleet Department, dated June

approval request:
Item: Kaeser SM15 duplex air compressor
Value: $37,095

Fund: General Fund/71- Equipment
Ordinance: Pursuant to § 5-84 Special purchase procedures. A/(5) Purchases from a sole
manufacturer, where it is determined to be more efficient and economical to
reduce costs of maintenance of additional repair parts, supplies or services.
Division of Public Works: Fleet, and the Purchasing Department respectfully requests your approval of
this contract.
Regards,
Amy Girard
Purchasing Manager
Cc: M Rush
C O'Connor
T Cummings
City of Nashua, Public Works Division
To: Board of Public Works Meeting Date: June 26, 2025
From: Michael Rush, Superintendent Fleet Department
Re: Purchase of a Kaeser SM15 Air Compressor
A. Motion: To approve the sole source purchase of a Kaeser SM15 duplex air compressor
from Able Air of Hudson, NH in the amount of $37,095. Funding will be through
Department 168 Solid Waste: Fund: General: Account Category: 71 Equipment
Attachments: Quote from Able Air of Hudson NH and Kaeser spec sheet
Discussion: This compressor will serve as the primary unit for our Fleet Maintenance Facility.
The current compressor is aging and struggling to meet the demands of our air-
powered tools, particularly during tire service operations. The new compressor
features a multi-unit design that offers both energy efficiency and operational
reliability. During periods of low demand, only one side of the unit operates to
conserve energy; during high-demand periods, a second unit automatically
engages to maintain adequate air supply. Additionally, the dual-unit configuration
provides built-in redundancy — in the event that one pump fails, the other will
continue operating, ensuring minimal disruption to daily operations.
Able Air is the only supplier of this compressor in the region and is located in
Hudson, NH. As a local supplier this would mean faster response time to service
requests and lower travel costs.
This compressor is also appropriately sized to be relocated to the future fleet
facility, resulting in a significant cost savings when that transition occurs. It
comes with a standard two-year warranty from the manufacture and continued
support from the vendor.

R-25-160
RESOLUTION
APPROVING AND AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF THE FIRST AMENDMENT
TO PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT FOR A DISCONTINUED PORTION
OF THE VETERANS MEMORIAL PARKWAY RIGHT-OF-WAY AND THE
EXECUTION OF AN INITIAL LEASE THEREOF (REDEVELOPMENT OF
MOHAWK TANNERY)
CITY OF NASHUA
In the Year Two Thousand and Twenty-Five
WHEREAS, the City is the owner of the land constituting the Veterans Memorial
Parkway (f/k/a Broad Street Parkway), situated in Nashua, Hillsborough County, New
Hampshire (the “Parkway”);
WHEREAS, in R-24-050, the Board of Aldermen authorized the sale of a portion of
the Parkway, which portion contains approximately 4.42 acres and is shown as the “Parkway
Parcel,” Lot 251, on a plan titled “Subdivision Plan Portion of Veterans Memorial Parkway
Nashua, New Hampshire” prepared by Hayner/Swanson, Inc. dated 20 April 2023, as revised
(the “Parkway Parcel”), to Blaylock Holdings, LLC, by designating Blaylock Holdings, LLC
as the selected proposer at the conclusion of the Request for Proposal process, and authorized
the execution of a Purchase and Sale Agreement; and
WHEREAS, on October 8, 2024, the Board of Aldermen approved a Petition for
Street Discontinuance for the Parkway Parcel, which petition has been or will be amended,
subject to the approval of the Board of Aldermen; and
WHEREAS, following the authorization in R-24-050, the City and Blaylock
Holdings, LLC entered into a Purchase and Sale Agreement dated June 6, 2024 (the
“Original Purchase and Sale Agreement”) for the conveyance of the Parkway Parcel to
Blaylock Holdings, LLC; and
RESOLUTION R-25-160
WHEREAS, in R-24-087, the Board of Aldermen resolved that the Parkway Parcel
is surplus property and shall be sold to Blaylock Holdings, LLC pursuant to the Original
Purchase and Sale Agreement and in accordance with any applicable ordinances and law;
and
WHEREAS, the City and Blaylock Holdings, LLC now desire to execute a First
Amendment to the Purchase and Sale Agreement, substantially in the form attached hereto
(the “First Amendment”), which will amend the Original Purchase and Sale Agreement; and
WHEREAS, the First Amendment provides that, prior to the acquisition of the
Parkway Parcel by Blaylock Holdings, LLC, the City shall lease the Parkway Parcel to
Blaylock Holdings, LLC upon the terms set forth in Lease, which shall be substantially in
the form which is attached as Exhibit B to the First Amendment (the “Lease”), and which
terms include a fair market rent in accordance with the fair market rent valuation for the
Parkway Parcel dated February 22, 2024, prepared by Bergeron Commercial Appraisal.
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Board of Aldermen of the City of
Nashua that the Mayor, with the assistance of the Office of Corporation Counsel, is hereby
authorized to execute the First Amendment and the Lease.
FURTHER RESOLVED that the Mayor is hereby authorized, with the assistance of
the Office of Corporation Counsel, to prepare and execute all necessary documents to effect
the purposes of the Original Purchase and Sale Agreement, as amended by the First
Amendment, including executing and delivering the Lease of the Parkway Parcel to Blaylock
Holdings, LLC and closing on the conveyance of the Parkway Parcel to Blaylock Holdings,
LLC.

FIRST AMENDMENT TO
PURCHASE AND SALE AGREEMENT
(Portion of Veterans Memorial Parkway Right-of-Way)
Effective Date: _________________, 2025
This First Amendment to Purchase And Sale Agreement (this “First Amendment”) is made
and entered into as of the Effective Date, by the City of Nashua, a New Hampshire municipal
corporation, with a principal address of City Hall, 229 Main Street, Nashua, New Hampshire
(mailing address: City of Nashua, P.O. Box 2019, Nashua, New Hampshire 03061-2019) (the
“Seller”) and Blaylock Holdings, LLC, a New Hampshire limited liability company, with a place
of business at 179 Amherst Street, Nashua, New Hampshire 03064 (the “Buyer”) (mailing address:
8 Pleasant Street, Suite A-2, South Natick Massachusetts, 01760).
Recitals
WHEREAS, the Buyer and the Seller entered into a Purchase and Sale Agreement dated
June 6, 2024 (the “Original Agreement”); and
WHEREAS, the Parties now desire to amend certain provisions of the Original Agreement
as set forth in this First Amendment, leaving all of the remaining terms and conditions unchanged.
Agreement
NOW, THEREFORE, in and for the mutual covenants set forth herein, the Buyer and the
Seller agree as follows:
Article I. Closing. The first sentence of Section 6 of the Original Agreement is hereby
deleted and replaced by the following text:
“The deed of the Parkway Parcel shall be executed and delivered by the Seller to the Buyer,
or its nominee or assignee, and possession of the Parkway Parcel shall be its nominee or assignee,
and the Buyer shall tender the Purchase Price to the Seller (in the form and manner set forth in
Section 4 above) on a date designated by the Buyer with at least thirty (30) days prior written
notice to the Seller (the “Closing”) at any time during the term of the Lease (defined in Section
11(A) below); provided that the Closing shall occur no later than thirty (30) days following the
issuance of the first building permit for a residential structure at the Project Site (defined in Section
10(C) below), and further provided that the Closing shall occur no later than (i) six (6) months
after substantial completion of the Remediation Work (defined in Section 10(A) below) for the
Project Site to the satisfaction of the United States Environmental Protection Agency (the “EPA”)
or (ii) three (3) years after the execution of the Lease (defined in Section 11(A) below), whichever
is earlier.”
Article II. Final Conditions Precedent. Section 9 of the Original Agreement is hereby
amended by deleting the entirety of the existing text and replacing it with the following text:
1
“A. The Buyer’s obligation to close on the purchase of the Parkway Parcel is subject to
the following final condition precedent (the “Final Condition Precedent”) being satisfied on or before
the expiration of the Secondary Period (defined below), which Final Condition Precedent runs to the
Buyer’s exclusive benefit:
(i) The Buyer (or its successor) has acquired the first building permit for a residential
structure at the Project Site.
B. No later than fifteen (15) days after the close of the Secondary Period, the Buyer shall
advise the Seller, in writing, as to whether or not the particular Final Condition Precedent referenced
in Section 9(A) above have been satisfied, not satisfied or waived, in whole or in part.
C. The term “Secondary Period” means the period of time commencing on June 6, 2024
and ending the last day of the term of the Lease, including the one-year extension that may be
exercised by the Buyer.
D. The Seller shall cooperate with the Buyer in such actions as may be requested by the
Buyer to seek satisfaction of the Final Condition Precedent. The Buyer shall pay for all costs and
expenses in seeking satisfaction of the Final Condition Precedent.”
Article III. Lease. A new Section 11 is hereby added to the Original Agreement. The
text of the new Section 11 is as follows:
“11. Lease.
A. On or prior to the date the Buyer closes on its purchase of the Project Site
(except for the Parkway Parcel) and effective as of the date the Buyer closes on its purchase of the
Project Site (except for the Parkway Parcel), the Seller and the Buyer shall enter into a lease of the
Parkway Parcel (the “Lease”). The form of the Lease shall be substantially as attached as Exhibit B
hereto, and shall include provisions which address the following:
(i) The leased premises shall constitute the Parkway Parcel;
(ii) The term of the Lease shall be two (2) years, unless extended by the
Buyer for an additional year;
(iii) The rent shall be Three Dollars ($3.00), paid in full upon the execution
of the Lease; and
(iv) During the term of the Lease, the Buyer may undertake all on-site
activities, necessary or desirable, to move and remove earth materials,
relocate earth materials and waste materials from the Parkway Parcel
to other portions of the Project Site, establish a entrance road and
staging area to implement the work, install and construct temporary
structures and enclosures related to the work, remove, relocate and
reconfigure stormwater management and drainage facilities and
2
installations and other utility components, install new stormwater
management and drainage facilities and installations and utility
components and other elements of the remediation and/or anticipated
development of the Parkway Parcel and the remainder of the Project
Site, and undertake all other activities necessary or desirable for the
remediation and/or anticipated development of the Parkway Parcel
and the remainder of the Project Site.
B. After satisfaction of the following conditions, the Seller and the Buyer shall
enter into the Lease:
(i) The Nashua City Planning Board has approved and recorded a
subdivision plan depicting the Parkway Parcel as a separate,
conveyable lot; and
(ii) The Buyer has closed on the acquisition of the remaining properties
which constitute the Project Site.
C. In the event the conditions set forth in Section 11(B) above have not been
satisfied by December 31, 2025 (the “Lease Conditions Date”), then the Buyer may (i) terminate
this Agreement and receive back the Deposit or (ii) extend the Lease Conditions Date (and the date
of the Closing) for an additional six (6) months, whereupon if the conditions set forth in Section
11(B) above have still not been satisfied, either party may terminate this Agreement.
D. Notwithstanding any other provisions of this Agreement, including, without
limitation, this Section 11, the Buyer shall not be obligated to enter into the Lease unless the Buyer
had closed on the acquisition of all of the other parcels of land which constitute the Project Site
(except for the Parkway Parcel).
E. Except for the condition referenced as item (i) in Section 11(B) above, the
Buyer may waive all or part of any of the provisions of this Section 11.
F. The parties shall cooperate to seek satisfaction of the conditions referenced
in Section 11(B) above, finalize the terms of the Lease and take all actions necessary to execute
the Lease. Notwithstanding the foregoing, by executing this Amendment and/or any applications
any federal, state, or local permits or approvals being sought by the Buyer in connection with (i)
the subdivision and discontinuance of the Parkway Parcel and (ii) the remediation and
redevelopment of the Project Site (the “Permits and Approvals”), or taking any action in
connection therewith, the Seller is not making a statement in favor or in opposition of any of the
Permits and Approvals.”
Article IV. Exhibit B (Lease). A new Exhibit B (Lease) in the form attached to this
First Amendment is hereby added to the Original Agreement.
Article V. Easements Benefiting Adjacent Land. A new Section 12 is hereby added to
the Original Agreement and all of the following sections and section references (throughout the
3
Original Agreement) are increased by two accordingly. The text of the new Section 12 is as
follows:
“12. Easements.
A. Section 19 of the MDA, as amended, requires the Buyer to grant to the
property owner(s) of Map 62, Lot 100 (land adjacent to the Parkway Parcel) an easement for access
and underground utility services. Simultaneously with the execution of the Lease, the Seller shall
grant to the property owner(s) of Map 62, Lot 100 an easement for access and underground utility
services, in the areas contemplated by the subdivision plans and site plans approved by the Nashua
City Planning Board for the Project, to serve Map 62, Lot 100 and other land adjacent to Map 62, Lot
100 owned by the Map 62, Lot 100 property owner(s).
B. The easement shall provide that the Seller shall have no obligation to construct
any access and utility facilities to serve Map 62, Lot 100 or adjacent land, all such obligations
remaining with the Buyer.
C. Such easement shall be granted by the Seller with Quitclaim (not Warranty)
covenants.
D. If, prior to the Closing, utility providers require the granting of easements to
serve the Project Site, the Seller will grant such easements on such forms as mutually acceptable to
the utility provider, the Seller, and the Buyer. Such easements shall not impose upon the City any
financial obligations or obligations to construct the utility facilities.
Article VI. Access. Subsection A of Section 17 of the Original Agreement (now
renumbered Section 19) is hereby amended by deleting the second sentence thereof.
Article VII. Easements. Section 18 of the Original Agreement (now renumbered
Section 20) is hereby amended by deleting the entirety of the existing text and replacing it with
the following text:
“20. Easements for Stormwater Management and Drainage.
A. At the Closing, if the existing stormwater management and drainage
installations on the Parkway Parcel are still in operation, the Seller may reserve easements for the
existing stormwater management and drainage installations, and access to repair, replace and
maintain the same, in connection with the Parkway until such time as the Buyer constructs
replacements therefore, which replacements must be approved by the Seller prior to a release of
the easement. With respect to the deed of the Parkway Parcel, the Seller may reserve an easement
for stormwater management and drainage installations constructed or to be constructed by the
Buyer on or under the Parkway Parcel, to benefit the Seller with respect to stormwater management
and drainage pertaining to the Parkway. At the Closing, immediately after the recording of the
deed of the Parkway Parcel to the Buyer, the Buyer shall execute and record a non-exclusive
easement for stormwater management and drainage installations in favor of the Seller to
4
accommodate stormwater and surface waters from the Veterans Memorial Parkway, in form and
substance reasonably acceptable to the Buyer and the Seller.”
B. At the Closing, immediately after the recording of the deed of the Parkway
Parcel and the easement referenced in Section 20(A) above, the Buyer shall execute and record in
favor of the Seller an Easement (Mohawk Tannery Redevelopment – Stormwater Management
Practices), in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the Buyer and the Seller.
Article VIII. Deposit. The Buyer and the Seller confirm that the Deposit (required
pursuant to Section 2 of the Original Agreement) has been paid and is held in escrow by the Escrow
Agent.
Article IX. City Approval. The Board of Aldermen approved the Original Agreement
by passage of R-24-050 on May 28, 2024 and R-24-087 on October 8, 2024. The Board of
Aldermen approved this First Amendment by passage of R-25-160 on _______________, 2025.
Article X. Defined Terms. All capitalized terms used in this First Amendment but not
defined herein have the meanings given to such terms in the Origina
